answer: Each identity request must pass through a narrow physical inlet where a bonded warden captures a fresh biometric; a public mirror of the issuer's ledger stores the hash. The issuer keeps an orchard of template hashes and rejects any second key whose template matches a stored one within a set distance, so extra identities require extra distinct humans, not extra accounts. With a fixed per-epoch reward r per credential and amortized per-epoch cost c, n identities gain n(r-c); sybils profit only while r>c. Spoofed biometrics, a captured warden, or false non-matches remain the vulnerability.
